changes: Adds the red-evidence v2 record and chain plane behind two new owner-gated commands. New modules under packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/: record-v2.ts (the four-operation v2 union with exhaustive per-operation field sets, always-present nullable chain fields, CANON recordDigest and specDigest, plus a fail-closed schema classifier), chain.ts (head resolution by both uniqueness conjuncts, the three integrity checks with a fork reason id distinct from the prior-digest one, the closed transition table, and cycle-safe transitive effective-head resolution), operation-key.ts (the three operation-key preimages, normalizedReason, and the deterministic OP-first12hex-seq record id), append.ts (the mandated pipeline order: derive key, dedupe, replay short-circuit, resolve head, transition legality, integrity checks, append; every append serialized under one per-story-per-target mkdir claim). types.ts widens RedEvidenceData.records to a mixed v1 and v2 array with the on-disk layout unchanged, and in the SAME commit proofstory.ts guards the v1 gate predicate so a non-v1 record can never reach observedFailure.trim(). store.ts classifies every record at load and fails closed with a typed RedEvidenceSchemaError on an unsupported schemaVersion. handlers/red-evidence.ts adds red_evidence_quarantine and red_evidence_recover with the reference-validation state machine, a derived approvedBy, a write-time expectedRedTargets membership gate, and the binding-freeze rule, and rejects a caller-supplied approvedBy. Both commands are wired through the full registration recipe (registry, command-catalog, command-policy, config, process-fact-levels, process-fact-registry, types union, agent-dispatch-registry, and the process-fact contract enumerations). tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.ts is registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands, and ten committed regression tests live under packages/main/tests/red/.
usage: Retire a red-evidence record and reinstate it, then run the committed chain smoke: node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_quarantine --storyId=B-xxxx --recordId=RED-ab12cd34ef56-1 --reason='superseded by the fixed assertion' ; node bin/lattice.js red_evidence_recover --storyId=B-xxxx --recordId=QUA-9f81ac2d40b7-2 --reason='quarantine was a mistake' ; node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.js
expectedOutcome: Running red_evidence_quarantine prints a chain receipt naming the new record id, its seq, the prior digest and a derived approvedBy of the form actor-at-session; red_evidence_recover does the same for the reinstatement; and node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.js prints a single OK line covering the v2 union, the byte-identical v1 enforce-gate guard, chain integrity, the transition table, operation keys, dedupe and replay ordering, the rejection matrix, the binding freeze, and the two-process race.
actualTranscript: node packages/main/dist/tasks/red-evidence-chain-smoke.js -> red-evidence-chain-smoke: OK - v2 union + section 0.4 omission/nullability; enforce-gate byte-identical v1 guard (RED signal A); chain head both conjuncts + three integrity checks with distinct reason ids; closed transition table + transitive cycle-safe effective head; operation-key + normalizedReason + deterministic id; dedupe/replay ordering + scoped dedupe + CONFLICT; full rejection matrix + retired byte-identical + forged approvedBy rejected + membership gate; section 1.1.3 binding-freeze/unfreeze/re-freeze; genuine 2-process mkdir-claim race -> one head (RED signal B); empty-records round-trip boundary case. node packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs -> five-scenario FULL-diagnostic sha256 = 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec, OK. node bin/lattice.js validate -> exit 0, 52 of 52 configured commands green, including the registered chain smoke.
outcomeDiff: No difference. The observed smoke line, the reproducible five-scenario digest, and the green validate run match the expected outcome.
limitations: none - fully covered, with one correction recorded openly below. Every claim is backed by a committed regression: the live enforce-gate crash class is proven differentially (a dist built from the pre-change tree throws a TypeError at observedFailure.trim, the current tree returns a typed RedEvidenceSchemaError), v1-verdict invariance is proven by packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs, which runs five v1-only scenarios through the real diagnostics and hashes the concatenated canonicalized FULL reports to sha256 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec - the pre-change tree produces the SAME digest, so no v1 verdict moved - the serialization claim is proven by a genuine two-process race, and the chain rules by a hashed rejection matrix. CORRECTION AND RETRACTION: an earlier version of this summary, and the first resolution text of finding F-005, cited sha256 71c267a0a7372e9679d00b84be2e2b3480151bfa88939bddcae251aa750d95bc as a verified five-scenario byte-identity proof. That value was reported by a subagent and is produced by NOTHING in this repository; the TEST-phase delivery reviewer caught it. It is retracted and replaced by the reproducible digest above, and the F-005 resolution record carries the same retraction. This story writes only the two control operations; the assertion envelope, matchers, run receipts and the process-spawning runner belong to later leaves W2d and W2e, as the frozen scope boundary states. A pre-existing defect on main, where a malformed versionless record still classifies as v1 and crashes the same predicate, was raised by the cross-host reviewer, confirmed identical on main, and filed as a separate session task (not a Lattice story) rather than folded in here.
pitfalls: Six reviewers - four Claude lanes plus a real codex CLI second host - produced fifteen findings across four rounds. The first ten were code: three Claude lanes independently converged on a HIGH where an unknown schemaVersion fell through to the v1 branch and crashed the LIVE enforce gate, and the codex host found four that all four Claude lanes missed (head consistency validated only on a dedupe hit; a null head from a malformed non-empty chain treated as settable; the binding-freeze decision racing across two different locks; a caller-supplied approvedBy silently ignored). The last five were about this story's OWN EVIDENCE, and they are the more instructive ones. A digest reported by a subagent was written into the summary and into a finding resolution as verified fact without anyone grepping for it - it existed nowhere in the repository. Several assertions placed the record under test AFTER an already-satisfying record, and because the production iterator uses Array.prototype.some, which short-circuits, those assertions could never fail; one of them lived in the smoke that lattice validate actually consumes. One note described a test case that did not exist, having been copy-pasted from a sibling note. Seventy-one of ninety-four notes cited line numbers of the compiled artifact, already stale and structurally guaranteed to re-stale on the next build. Rules for the next person: grep for any digest or count before asserting it; require every RED-style assertion to be demonstrated FAILING against the pre-change tree rather than merely passing on the fixed one; anchor evidence notes to a source file plus a durable locator, never a line number; and treat honestly labelling an assertion as vacuous as insufficient - make it genuine or remove it. Process lessons: probing a blocked gate by re-running story_advance trips the convergence breaker at three repeats, so call it once and read the whole blocker list; quorum_submit validates each lane pass's prompt envelope against the changed-file set, so merge main BEFORE running the lanes that feed the quorum, not merely before the quorum; and when several sessions share one machine, lattice validate can hit its 900 second cap purely from lock contention, so wait for a quiet window rather than reading the abort as a failure.
